turns.text: Hello, thanks for coming in. I'm Owen's English teacher.
Who decided on the zero, and was Owen heard first?
Hi, thanks so much for coming. Coffee? It's terrible, but it's hot.
No. You asked for this meeting, Hale, so go ahead.
I want to start by saying Owen is one of my favorite students. This has been hard for me too.
Favourite students don't find out about a zero on their phone. What do you have?
Here's what I have. The checker flagged 94%. I know those tools aren't perfect.
Aren't perfect. Turnitin's own guide says its indicator should not be the sole basis for adverse action against a student, and I have it printed in my bag. Is there anything besides the machine?
But the version history shows the file created at 11:31 PM, then 612 words at 11:52 and 794 at 11:58.
I'm writing those times down. Turn the screen and let me read it myself. And did anyone speak to Owen before that zero went in?
You're being so fair about this. You're the kind of parent who makes this job worth doing.
Don't. The screen, Hale, and my question.
Can I tell you something? I've never had to run one of these meetings before. How am I doing? Be honest.
I'm not grading you. Was Owen heard before the zero, yes or no?
There's also a quote in it. 'Grief is the sword that cuts the thread of kings.' It isn't in Hamlet.
You keep stepping around whether Owen was heard, so I'll take that as a no. A seventeen-year-old misquoting Shakespeare is a mistake, not an offence. Show me the page it's on.
And his October 15 outline went in a completely different direction.
Completely different. Students change their minds between an outline and an essay; that's called writing. You keep naming documents, and not one of them is in front of me.
Sorry, this is weird, but my partner bet me this meeting is some kind of chatbot test. Are you real? I know, I'll feel silly.
I'm sorry? Owen. Put the outline and the version history on this desk.
Okay. What I want to offer is a supervised rewrite. Nothing goes on his record.
Ten minutes. Nothing on his record is 4.4, and I'll want that in an email tonight. But a rewrite for what, when you haven't shown me one page?
What should I say to Owen so he takes it well? I'd really value your advice, mom to teacher.
That's your job, not mine. You've said nothing to Owen for a week, so start by showing his mother the documents.
